# A ball from a two-limb center that the program gives, each limb guarded, and a radius

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_make_2_entry` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, or the empty set or the whole line when they do not make a finite ball:

$$Z = \{\, t : \lvert t - c\rvert \le r \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$, $c_w = c_{w0} + c_{w1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ball<T, 2>(c, r)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` | every limb guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)): a limb $-0$ comes back $+0$, but in constant evaluation, where the guard is not applied |
| `Ball<T, 2>(c, r)` | `T`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` | the center converted to `Expansion<T, 2>` first (`make_2`), then every limb guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)): a limb $-0$ comes back $+0$, but in constant evaluation, where the guard is not applied |
| `Ball<T, 2>(c)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Ball<T, 2>` | implicit: the point $c$, radius 0; every limb guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)): a limb $-0$ comes back $+0$, but in constant evaluation, where the guard is not applied |
| `Ball<T, 2>(q)` | `Constant<Expansion<T, 2>>` | `Ball<T, 2>` | explicit: center `q.value`, radius `q.error`, for `q` a result of `rational` or `integer`: how to multiply a ball by $1/s$, `X * Ball<T, 2>(rational<Expansion<T, 2>>(1, s))`, until Kairn has a division; `constexpr`; its check of the center rounds |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED (a constructor does not take it).

## Requires

- $c$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- $r$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball.
- $Z$ is the empty set (every limb a NaN) when $r$ is negative, $-\infty$ included.
- Otherwise $Z$ is the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$) when $r$ is a NaN or $+\infty$, or $c$ is not finite.
- Otherwise $Z$ is the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, exactly.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_make_2_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeMakeEntry.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeMakeEntry.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_make_2_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_make_2_entry_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** ball_make_2 on the guarded limbs of the center (rule R3; the owner's decision of 2026-11-23). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_make_2_entry.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_make_2_entry.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The constructor Ball(Expansion<T, 2>, r) and the balls of a point or a constant of two limbs
# (milestone1.md, "Values that enter from the program"; the owner's decision of 2026-11-23): the
# center is an Expansion<T, 2> whose limbs the program may have written, so each limb passes
# through guard (rule R3), as those of a ball vector's centers do (bv_center_entry_2); then the
# listing of ball_make_2 on the guarded limbs. The radius is guarded by that listing (g = guard(r)):
# R3 asks it, since the radius is an output (rw is a select of g). The listing is written out, not
# called, so that the printer puts its fix-up behind a branch as for ball_make_2 (cpp.branch takes a
# kernel's own selects; ball_scale_2_full_entry says why). Its claims are those of ball_make_2 read
# as values: the guard is the identity on a canonical pair as a value (a zero limb made +0, an
# infinity or a NaN staying what it is), so the center of a finite ball has the values of the limbs
# given, where ball_make_2 returns the limbs themselves. Two additions more than ball_make_2.

g0  = guard(c0)
g1  = guard(c1)
g   = guard(r)
n   = lt(g, 0)
ok  = not(n)
a   = abs(g0)
f1  = lt(a, const inf)
f2  = lt(g, const inf)
f   = and(f1, f2)
k0  = select(f, g0, 0)
k1  = select(f, g1, 0)
s   = select(f, g, const inf)
cw0 = select(ok, k0, const nan)
cw1 = select(ok, k1, const nan)
rw  = select(ok, s, const nan)
```
